the perioperative care of the obese patient is a challenge for the anesthesiology team.

obesity is a complex disease with a multifaceted etiology, that obesity has a significant negative impact on health, and that obesity is associated with a high prevalence of comorbidities, which are also associated with increased morbidity and mortality.
Obesity, its complications, and its treatment have great importance for the anaesthesiologist.

the anesthetic management of obese patients and its complications.
the anesthetic management of the obese patient and with the perioperative care of the morbidly obese patient.
the perioperative management and care of obese subjects.

obesity should be considered a risk factor for the anesthetist, but not an absolute contraindication to anesthesia.
obesity is a major risk factor for perioperative morbidity.
the anesthesiologists must be aware of the pathophysiological problems of obesity and their consequences in order to provide the best perioperative management for these patients.

the obese patient should be considered as any other patient with a special attention to his pathophisiology, to his perioperative management and to the post-operative care.
obesity should not be a contraindication for surgery.

the perioperative anesthesiological care of the obese patient should be based on a multidisciplinary team approach.
